findings.issue_text: Permission check in addGuests.handler.ts uses `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` instead of `||`, wrongly rejecting team admins
getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and EventManager use the acting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, so calendar/video updates run against the wrong account
sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) passes the raw `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests`, so filtered-out and blacklisted emails still receive emails
Blacklist comparison is case-mismatched: env list is lowercased but incoming guest email is not normalized, allowing `Blocked@Example.com` to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS
Duplicate detection `guest === attendee.email` is case-sensitive and there is no server-side dedupe within the guests array, allowing duplicate attendee rows
addGuests.schema.ts guests array has no `.max()` bound, allowing thousands of attendees/emails per request (email amplification/DoS vector)
No check on booking state: cancelled, rejected, or past bookings accept new guests and dispatch booking emails with meeting link/ICS
Seat limits (seatsPerTimeSlot) are never enforced, so guests can exceed capacity; with seatsShowAttendees === false the emails also leak the full attendee list
Check-then-insert with no transaction or unique constraint on (bookingId, email), so concurrent addGuests calls create duplicate attendees and duplicate emails
packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx imports from the `@calcom/ui` barrel that re-exports itself, creating a circular import that risks undefined-component render errors
No tests for the new tRPC handler covering the authorization matrix, blacklist filtering, and dedupe behavior
organizer-add-guests-email.ts accesses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` without a guard, throwing if attendees is empty
AddGuestsDialog.tsx builds `message` as an always-truthy template string, making the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback dead code and showing users raw error codes
AddGuestsDialog.tsx never resets `isInvalidEmail` when the user edits the email fields, leaving the error banner visible after correction
Error handler `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") }` discards the error, making email delivery failures undiagnosable

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and EventManager use the acting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, so calendar/video updates run against the wrong account

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler fetches the booking including the organizer user and their `credentials` (`include: { user: { include: { credentials: true }}}`), but then ignores those and instead does `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and constructs `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user` is the acting/authed user (could be a team admin/owner or even an attendee per the permission checks). Since `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will run using the credentials passed into `EventManager`, this makes the calendar update operate under the acting user's integrations rather than the booking organizer's. That is a concrete correctness defect introduced by the diff: updates can fail (no credentials) or target the wrong external calendar account when someone other than the organizer adds guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.schema.ts guests array has no `.max()` bound, allowing thousands of attendees/emails per request (email amplification/DoS vector)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.schema.ts`, `guests` is defined as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound. The new `addGuestsHandler` then processes the entire array: it filters and builds `guestsFullDetails`, performs a `createMany` insert, updates calendar attendees, and triggers `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which iterates over `calendarEvent.attendees` and queues an email per attendee. With no `.max()` (and no other limit visible in the diff), a single request can supply an extremely large `guests` array, leading to large DB writes + calendar updates + mass email sends (amplification/DoS vector). This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No check on booking state: cancelled, rejected, or past bookings accept new guests and dispatch booking emails with meeting link/ICS

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` fetches a booking by `id` and, if found and the caller is authorized, unconditionally updates `attendees` and then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. There is no validation of booking state (e.g., cancelled/rejected) or timing (e.g., `startTime` already in the past) before mutating the booking and sending ICS/email notifications that can include video call data. This makes the finding (no state check; emails/ICS still sent) directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Seat limits (seatsPerTimeSlot) are never enforced, so guests can exceed capacity; with seatsShowAttendees === false the emails also leak the full attendee list
Check-then-insert with no transaction or unique constraint on (bookingId, email), so concurrent addGuests calls create duplicate attendees and duplicate emails

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code reads the current attendees via prisma.booking.findFirst(...include: {attendees:true}) and then later inserts new attendees via prisma.booking.update(...attendees.createMany) based on that earlier snapshot. There is no transaction tying the read and write together, and no server-side de-duplication against other in-flight requests; therefore two concurrent addGuests calls for the same booking/email can both conclude the email is absent and both insert it. Whether the DB has a unique constraint is not shown in this diff, but the application logic as added is a classic check-then-insert race that can create duplicates (or at least produce nondeterministic behavior) unless a DB constraint exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx imports from the `@calcom/ui` barrel that re-exports itself, creating a circular import that risks undefined-component render errors
No tests for the new tRPC handler covering the authorization matrix, blacklist filtering, and dedupe behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `addGuests` tRPC mutation/handler and UI, but it does not add any test files. However, the finding claims there are “no tests” covering the new handler’s behavior, which is not verifiable from the diff alone (tests could exist elsewhere or be added in a separate change). Also, lack of tests is a process/coverage concern rather than a concrete functional/security defect introduced by the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: organizer-add-guests-email.ts accesses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` without a guard, throwing if attendees is empty

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the subject line interpolates `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. If `this.calEvent.attendees` is an empty array, `this.calEvent.attendees[0]` is `undefined` and accessing `.name` will throw at runtime. The diff does not add any guard or enforce (within this file/template) that `attendees` is non-empty, so the unsafe access is a real, directly verifiable defect in the added code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx builds `message` as an always-truthy template string, making the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback dead code and showing users raw error codes

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, onError builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then calls `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. A template literal always produces a string; with the hardcoded `": "` it will be non-empty even when `err.data?.code` is undefined, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is effectively unreachable. This also means users may see raw/error codes like `BAD_REQUEST: ...` or `undefined: ...` in the toast.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx never resets `isInvalidEmail` when the user edits the email fields, leaving the error banner visible after correction

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails in `handleAdd()`. After that, the only places that reset it are the Cancel button handler (`setIsInvalidEmail(false)`) and implicitly on a successful mutation (dialog closes and state resets, but `isInvalidEmail` is not explicitly reset there). The `MultiEmail` component is rendered with `setValue={setMultiEmailValue}` only; there is no `onChange`/wrapper logic to clear `isInvalidEmail` when the user edits the email inputs. Therefore, once the error banner is shown, it will remain visible even after the user corrects the emails, until they click Add again or cancel/close, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error handler `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") }` discards the error, making email delivery failures undiagnosable

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the call to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch`, and the `catch` only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging `err` and without rethrowing. This verifiably discards the actual error details, making it difficult to diagnose why email sending failed (only a generic message is emitted).
